items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Stable isotope analyses of freshwater mollusc carbonate can record environmental conditions at the time of mineralisation, yet this technique remains underused in British Middle Pleistocene fluvial sequences, despite the abundance of fossil shell material in these deposits. We present new δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O and δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C measurements from calcitic
                    <jats:italic>Bithynia tentaculata</jats:italic>
                    opercula and aragonitic
                    <jats:italic>Valvata piscinalis</jats:italic>
                    shells from fluvial sediments at Swanscombe, in the Lower Thames Valley, correlated with the Hoxnian Interglacial (MIS 11c). We assess whether isotope values show sustained change through units correlated with the MIS 11c thermal maximum, and whether inter‐taxon differences provide evidence for seasonal differences in carbonate mineralisation. Across the dataset (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 173), δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O and δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C values fall within the range expected for a groundwater‐influenced temperate lowland river system. Sample medians show little systematic stratigraphic change, indicating limited variation in environmental conditions during the sampled intervals of fluvial deposition. After accounting for mineralogy, the inter‐taxon δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O offset is consistent with differences in growth season, whereas the δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C offset likely reflects species‐specific differences in microhabitat and carbon incorporation. The Swanscombe isotope record therefore supports fully temperate MIS 11c conditions, with little evidence for sustained long‐term thermal change during the sampled intervals. Instead, the paired‐taxon record suggests that seasonal signals may be preserved even where mean environmental conditions remained relatively stable. These results demonstrate the value of paired‐taxon stable isotope analysis in fluvial archives for reconstructing climate stability and identifying seasonal signals during Middle Pleistocene interglacials.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《斯旺斯科姆淡水腹足类碳酸盐稳定同位素分析：对MIS 11c时期气候稳定性与季节性的启示》：研究利用英国下泰晤士河谷斯旺斯科姆河相沉积中Bithynia tentaculata方解石口盖与Valvata piscinalis文石壳的氧、碳稳定同位素，检验MIS 11c热盛期环境条件是否持续变化及属间差异能否反映矿化季节差异，结果支持该时期为完全温带条件、长…
items.title: Stable isotope analysis of freshwater gastropod carbonates from Swanscombe: Insights into climate stability and seasonality during MIS 11c

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We present new multi-proxy data investigating major environmental transitions over the last 5 kyr BP, based on a sediment core retrieved from the Gulf of Gdańsk (SE Baltic Sea). Between 5 and 1.5 kyr BP, the bay experienced low-energy depositional conditions, which were disrupted around 4 kyr BP, likely due to intensified storm activity and reduced river discharge, potentially linked to the formation of a coastal spit that altered sediment transport patterns. The benthic foraminiferal assemblage during this interval was monospecific, dominated by
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Cribroelphidium clavatum</jats:italic>
                    , a euryhaline species well adapted to brackish conditions. Low benthic δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O values indicated a notable freshening of the Gulf of Gdańsk between 3 and 1.7 kyr BP. A more pronounced shift in the depositional environment occurred around 1.4 kyr BP, when salinity drops and possible hypoxia disrupted benthic habitats. These changes led to the local disappearance of benthic foraminifera assemblages, previously dominated by
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Cribroelphidium clavatum</jats:italic>
                    . Although environmental conditions improved around 0.9 kyr BP, benthic foraminiferal communities did not re-establish, likely due to persistent low salinity and bottom hypoxia conditions.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《格但斯克湾（波罗的海南部）过去5000年古环境变化的首个有孔虫记录与多指标重建》：基于沉积岩芯的多指标数据，重建该湾5千年来主要环境转变，包括约4千年前的沉积扰动、3至1.7千年前的显著淡化，以及约1.4千年前盐度下降与可能缺氧导致底栖有孔虫消失。适合关注波罗的海古环境与有孔虫生态的读者。

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Hester Site (22MO569) is a multi‐component archeological site located in northeastern Mississippi with occupations spanning the Late Pleistocene through Holocene chronozones. The site was initially investigated by the Mississippi Department of Archives and History (MDAH) in the 1970s and is notable for being a rare example of a stratified, open‐air site dating to the Late Pleistocene in the American Southeast. However, while the temporally diagnostic artifacts appear to be in stratigraphic order, previously reported radiocarbon dates are too recent to be consistent with accepted regional chronology. Here, we apply methods derived from site formation theory to artifact and sediment data from the 2017–2025 field seasons conducted by Mississippi State University to evaluate the degree to which postdepositional processes have impacted the deposits at the site. Specifically, we use particle size analysis, loss‐on‐ignition (LOI), six new radiocarbon dates, artifact orientation (dip/strike), refits and a spatial analysis to argue for the presence of multiple Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene occupations. We contend that multiple cultural and natural formation processes have affected the deposits at the Hester site, yet the site is a valuable datapoint for understanding how people adapted to a warming climate at the Pleistocene‐Holocene transition in the American Southeast.</jats:p>
